stem.en: Alcohol holds about 18 drops on the coin. Water holds 31. Alcohol has one O-H group per molecule; water has two. Kabir says alcohol "should be half as sticky, so 15 drops". What is the better reading?

text.en: Alcohol can make hydrogen bonds but fewer per molecule than water, so it holds itself together less strongly. The count is not exactly half, because a drop's shape depends on more than one thing, but the direction is right.

feedback.en: Any molecule with a hydrogen on an oxygen or nitrogen can make one. Alcohol's O-H does. That is why it beats oil so easily.

text.en: Alcohol is lighter, so it spills sooner.

feedback.en: Lighter would mean a taller dome before it spills, not a shorter one. Weight is not what limits the pile.

text.en: Alcohol evaporates, so the drops are lost.

feedback.en: It does evaporate, but the test counts drops added before the dome breaks, and the dome breaks long before much has gone.

explanation.en: More hydrogen-bonding sites per molecule means a tighter hold. Water's two hydrogens and two lone pairs give it more than any other small molecule.
